t: A federation of East Slavic principalities ruled by the Rurikid dynasty from Kiev, on the river route from the Baltic to Byzantium.
Vladimir the Great's conversion around 988 brought Orthodox Christianity, Cyrillic writing and Byzantine art to Rus'.
Fragmented into rival principalities after 1132, it was destroyed by the Mongols, who sacked Kiev in 1240.
dyk: More than a thousand letters written on birch bark, found at Novgorod since 1951, show ordinary townspeople of Rus' writing everyday notes, debts and family messages.
ev: Oleg of Novgorod takes Kiev and makes it his seat
Oleg concludes a trade treaty with the Byzantine Empire
Sviatoslav I destroys the Khazar Khaganate
Vladimir the Great accepts Byzantine Christianity
Yaroslav the Wise becomes sole ruler and defeats the Pechenegs
The Council of Liubech confirms each prince's hereditary patrimony
Andrei Bogolyubsky of Vladimir-Suzdal sacks Kiev
Batu Khan's Mongol army storms and sacks Kiev

f.successor: Rus' principalities (Vladimir-Suzdal, Galicia-Volhynia, Novgorod Republic) under the Golden Horde
